name: Leche La Vaca
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (FS Road 7601 off Icicle Creek Road), hike the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599): gentle forest walking along Mountaineer Creek for 1.5 miles to a log-bridge crossing, then right at the Lake Stuart Trail junction, then a final boulder-moraine push to the lake outlet — about 4 miles, 2,280 ft gain, 2.5-3 hours. Top off water here, the last reliable source. Continue around toward the lake's south/east shore onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail, gaining steep talus and heather to about 400 ft above the lake (30-40 min; a slope that holds wet snow into July and has produced serious slips). Cut climber's-left off the Aasgard trail through a dense slide-alder/heather band (15-20 minutes of real bushwhacking) to the base of the gully system below Colchuck Balanced Rock. Leche La Vaca starts in this same base gully area on the left side of the wall, near Scarface; the final approach scramble to the wall is loose 3rd/4th class terrain. Figure 3.5-4 hours car-to-base overall.
